provenance.paper: Hwang et al., 'Stable real-space invariants and topology beyond symmetry indicators', Nat. Commun. 17, 8564 (2026)
provenance.omitted_reason: space groups with only one site-symmetry irrep in a unit cell, for which the unique SRSI is determined by the number of bands (the caption of the supplement's SRSI tables states the omission and this reason)
notes: The site-symmetry representation vector p of the paper runs over ALL Wyckoff positions; an EBR basis carries only the maximal ones, and only those maximal site irreps whose induced band representation is elementary. Terms with no EBR column are kept in full with column=null, and say which case they are: maximal=false is a non-maximal Wyckoff position, maximal=true with ebr=false is a maximal position whose induced band representation is composite. Restricting Theta to the EBR columns is exact for any p supported there, which is every p this package builds.

The label elimination: at each maximal position the supplement's spellings and irreptables' EBR labels are matched directly, and what is left over is paired only when exactly one label remains on each side. `label_aliases` reports every pairing that was forced this way and `composite_site_irreps` the supplement spellings that had nothing to pair with. Both are measured, not declared.

Column indices index ebr_data(grey group)['ebrs'] of pythtqc, whose rows are transported into this package's e^{-ik.t} convention; the (label, Wyckoff letter) key list is stored beside them so a loader can check the installed tables still agree.
Indicator coefficients are exact [numerator, denominator] pairs: the supplement's SI rows carry fractional coefficients (for example SG 147 and SG 162 without SOC).

Every indicator carries a DERIVED row beside the printed one: the unique rational a with a.Theta0 = c.BR, c being irreptables' named form of the same name (transported and checked to vanish on this group's EBRs) or, for a group with a single elementary divisor, its own Smith coordinate. `relation` says how the printed row compares -- equal, equivalent (same function on a Z-basis of {BS}, mod n) or different. `derived` is null for the rows whose name has no counterpart in either vocabulary, with the reason on `derived_note`.
